intro: The weather station on the summit has been automated for forty years. This morning its printer woke up and produced something that is definitely not a forecast: a sheaf of old-style telegrams, each bearing a single line of weather jargon followed by one stray, clearly out-of-place letter at the bottom margin. The forecasters gathered round, passing the pages down the table like parish notices, one of them remarking that the margins look like a roll call taken in the wet. The station log confirms the machine has only ever printed observations, never prose, yet every sheet is dated today, and none of them predicts rain. One junior observer has begun carefully clipping each odd letter onto a strip of card, saying nothing, her tongue between her teeth. Out of habit, the senior forecaster checked the barometer twice, though it has not moved in decades.
echo: Dorothy's house left Kansas in one.

puzzles.title: Veering
puzzles.flavor: Only one page survived. It was the only page anyone needed. Start from the end; that's where it started.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

hints: Once every theme word is found, is anything left unclaimed? Read it in order.
Find the theme words; the letters no word uses, read row by row, are the answer.
The hidden words are: BREEZE, DEWPOINT, DROUGHT, FROST, GALE, HAIL, HUMIDITY, MIST, RADAR, SQUALL.
